## ACT plots

ACT denotes the asthma-control score used in the code. In the visit panels, each point is an observed participant score; horizontal spreading helps reveal overlapping points. The trajectory plots connect a participant's recorded visits. A connecting segment does not provide measurements between visits. A separate scatterplot compares self-reported adherence with interval app-recorded PDC; agreement between these measures is a different question from whether the intervention changed either one.

```{r}
#| label: act-plots
#| eval: false
```

## Count outcome plots

The loop creates one plot per count outcome and saves it under that outcome's name. Each point is a participant-level count. The plot makes skewness, many zeros and unusually large counts visible; it neither adjusts for follow-up nor establishes that an unusual value is an error. `aes()` maps variables to positions and colours, while `geom_*()` chooses marks. The [ggplot2 introduction](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/articles/ggplot2.html) explains this layering [@ggplotintro].

```{r}
#| label: count-outcome-plots
#| eval: false
```

## Medication plots

Rescue counts are shown on ordinary and logarithmic scales. A log scale makes multiplicative differences easier to see, but zero cannot be shown on that scale and may be omitted with a warning. Compare it with the ordinary-scale plot before interpreting the distribution. Controller PDC plots show participant proportions; their interpretation depends on the denominator described in [Derive medication outcomes](03_derive_medication_outcomes.qmd#controller-day-grid).

## Mixed model plots overall

Faint trajectories show recorded measurements, while prominent points and lines show model-estimated group means. Error bars are confidence intervals for those means, not the range containing most individual scores. The table under the plot, "Observed, n", counts the participants with the outcome recorded at each visit; it is not necessarily the model sample if predictors are missing. Follow-up p-values marked with a dagger test differences in change from baseline, so they do not simply test the visible gap between the two means at that visit.

What the plotted means, error bars and p-values come from is in [How this code does it](methods_in_this_code.qmd#estimates-and-plots).

```{r}
#| label: mixed-model-plots-overall
#| eval: false
```

## Mixed model plots subgroups

The loops add one subgroup at a time and return plots in a list indexed by population, outcome and subgroup. The within-panel p-values and between-subgroup p-values answer different questions. At follow-up the latter concern differences in the change-from-baseline arm contrast. Read the [interaction explanation](methods_interaction_p_values.qmd) before comparing a small p-value in one panel with a large one in another.

The script creates plot objects in memory and does not export them. The website displays this code without showing participant-derived plots.

Each subgroup level has its own column with its own participants, side by side on the same scale. Under the panels, one row of p-values tests the contrast within each level and another, under each level after the first, tests its difference from the first level; see [How to read the trajectory figure](methods_reading_trajectory_figure.qmd), [How this code does it](methods_in_this_code.qmd#estimates-and-plots) and [What a p-value for interaction means](methods_interaction_p_values.qmd).
